subject: RFP Clarification: Responsibility Matrix and Evaluation Ownership for AI Risk Annex
messages:
From: Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@regalhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: RegalHealth Procurement <procurement@regalhealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarifications on RFP Annex (AI Risk) - responsibility and eval ownership

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the quick turn on the initial RFP response. The procurement team asked for a couple of clarifications specific to the AI Risk Annex so we can complete our scoring rubric:

1) Responsibility matrix: the template asks for a RACI-style table that shows who is responsible for ongoing evaluations, regression testing, and corrective action. Can Redwood provide the proposed RACI for (a) initial onboarding tests, (b) periodic regression, and (c) incident-triggered re-evaluation?

2) Evidence and ownership: for each assurance item (e.g., model drift monitoring, prompt/regression test artifacts, NIST AI RMF mappings), do you expect Redwood to be the primary evidence owner, or will RegalHealth need to retain/produce artifacts on your behalf?

3) Frequency and sampling: any guidance on recommended sampling/cadence for regression (esp. for high-risk/clinical-assist workflows)? The RFP scoring team wants a concrete number to compare vendors.

We'd appreciate a short written clarification and any templates you can share (responsibility matrix or sampling plan). If it's easier to discuss, I can set a 30-minute slot this Friday.

Thanks,
Sonia Patel
Senior Sourcing Manager, RegalHealth
(Attachment: RFP_Annex_AI_Risk_Sections.pdf)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@regalhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifications on RFP Annex (AI Risk) - responsibility and eval ownership

Hi Sonia — great questions, thanks for the detail. Summary answers below and I attached a draft responsibility matrix and a short sampling plan for your review. Happy to hop on a call if helpful.

A. Responsibility matrix (high-level)
- Initial onboarding tests: Redwood = Owner (we run onboarding evals, provide test reports and baseline metrics); RegalHealth = Account Reviewer (validates domain-specific test coverage).
- Periodic regression: Shared (Redwood runs scheduled regressions and delivers reports; RegalHealth retains final acceptance and can run parallel validations).
- Incident-triggered re-evaluation: Redwood = Owner for triage and initial regression; RegalHealth = Owner for remediation decisions and production gating.

B. Evidence ownership
- Redwood provides the technical artefacts we control: model binary hashes, inference logs (configurable retention), evaluation harness outputs, test scripts, and aggregated metrics dashboards.
- RegalHealth will retain business artifacts (labeling decisions, clinical adjudication notes, acceptance sign-offs). For formal audits we typically package a combined evidence bundle; Redwood can host the technical portion in a secure link or provide encrypted export.

C. Sampling & cadence (provisional)
- High-risk (clinical-assist / safety-critical): stratified sampling targeting at least 5% of production requests monthly, with focused edge-case oversampling (minimum 2k checks/month or 5% whichever is higher).
- Medium-risk (decision-support): quarterly regression covering representative intents and top-traffic buckets (approx 1% sample minimum).
- Low-risk (informational): on-deploy + spot checks.

Other notes: we map our regression outputs to NIST AI RMF subcategories (Governance: inventory & roles; Measurement: evaluation metrics; Monitor: ongoing performance monitoring). For EU AI Act high-risk classification we provide the artifacts required for conformity assessments (transparency records, risk assessments, and eval summaries).

Attachments included: redwood-assurance-matrix-v1.xlsx (draft RACI), redwood-eval-sampling-plan.pdf (sampling rationale & worked examples).

Proposed next step: if those attachments look good, we can convert the draft RACI into a short SOW line item (Redwood-run regression cadence) and include it in the annex.

Would Friday 10:00–10:30 PT work for a quick alignment call?

Best,
Marcus Lin
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redwood-assurance-matrix-v1.xlsx)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-06T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: proposed thresholds and owners for RegalHealth RFP (do not forward)

Marcus / Priya — internal notes ahead of the call with RegalHealth.

1) Sampling specifics (technical)
- We should propose a default stratification by intent, client cohort (tenant), and score-risk band. For clinical-assist flows we recommend: monthly stratified sample = max(2000 checks, 5% of prod volume). For edge-case buckets (rare intents flagged by model uncertainty), escalate sample fraction to 15% of that bucket.

2) Responsibility split (detailed)
- Redwood-run tasks: test harness execution, baseline metric computation (accuracy/ROUGE/clinical-F1 where applicable), drift signal detection, KV/prefix cache reproducibility checks, and packaging technical artifacts.
- Customer-run tasks: domain labeling, clinical adjudication, acceptance sign-off, and escalation decisions (we provide suggested remediation options).

3) Evidence retention & access
- Technical artifact retention: 12 months by default, extendable to contract length. Audit exports: consolidated zip with hashes + evaluation reports.

4) Automation & integrations
- Use Redwood Console eval hooks + webhooks to push results to customer S3 / secure share for their records. For customers with Private deployment, we support on-prem artifact collection.

Action items for call:
- Marcus: confirm the sample numbers and the proposed RACI in the draft matrix.
- Priya: be prepared to align on SOW language (billing cadence for Redwood-run regressions).
- Neha: prepare a one-pager mapping NIST AI RMF categories to Redwood telemetry and the eval outputs (I attached internal-eval-ops-workflow.md).

Neha
Head of Applied ML — Redwood Inference
(Attachment: internal-eval-ops-workflow.md)

Subject: Re: Clarifications on RFP Annex (AI Risk) - responsibility and eval ownership

Hi Sonia — following our internal alignment, please find a consolidated response and attachments.

1) Responsibility matrix (attached) — key points: Redwood will be the primary owner for running technical regressions (onboarding, scheduled, and incident-triggered) and delivering technical reports / artefacts. RegalHealth remains the owner for clinical adjudication and production gating decisions. The attached XLSX has a RACI per line-item to drop into the Annex.

2) Evidence ownership & packaging — Redwood will supply: model hashes, evaluation harness logs, aggregated metrics dashboards, raw (anonymized) test vectors used in regressions, and a reproducible runbook for how tests were executed. For formal audits we will assemble a combined evidence bundle; we can host the technical portion behind a secure download link or provide an encrypted export.

3) Sampling & cadence (final proposed numbers)
- High-risk (clinical-assist): monthly stratified sampling (min 5% of requests or 2k checks).
- Medium-risk: quarterly sampling (min 1% or 500 checks).
- Incident-triggered: full regression on defined impacted slices; turnaround target 72 hours for initial triage report, 7 business days for full re-eval.

4) Mapping to NIST & EU AI Act
- NIST AI RMF: we map our outputs to the core functions (Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover) and provide a subcategory mapping spreadsheet (see Drive link).
- EU AI Act: for high-risk systems we provide the supporting documentation typically requested by conformity assessors (transparency records, risk assessments, evaluation artifacts). Final conformity assessments remain the responsibility of the customer / certifying body but Redwood will provide the technical evidence.

Attachments: redwood-assurance-matrix-v1.xlsx; redwood-eval-sampling-plan.pdf.

Next steps: if the draft RACI and sampling plan meet your needs we can (a) insert a short SOW clause that makes Redwood-run regression an optional add-on with defined cadence and acceptance criteria, or (b) mark it as customer-owned with Redwood providing the tooling and runbooks. Which approach does procurement prefer for scoring?

Happy to discuss — I can take the call Friday 10:00 PT as proposed (or we can move it).

Best regards,
Marcus Lin
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
